t: Knowledge Propagation Tracker: a plain-language overview
title: Knowledge Propagation Tracker: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Propagation Tracker does and why archives need it. A knowledge propagation tracker follows a fact as it travels: which articles quoted it, which datasets copied it, which books reprinted it. When the fact gets corrected, the tracker finds every place the old version lives so the correction can follow. Facts travel; this tool follows them.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Propagation Tracker works
title: How the Knowledge Propagation Tracker works
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Propagation Tracker does and why archives need it. Real trackers build a reuse graph from citation links, text-reuse detection (near-duplicate passage matching), and dataset derivation records, then run forward traversals from any fact to list every downstream reuse. When a correction lands, the tracker computes the correction cascade — all affected downstream nodes — and reports which have been updated and which still carry the old version. Each reuse edge cites its evidence (quote, citation, derivation log).
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Knowledge Propagation Tracker works: the deep tour
title: How the Knowledge Propagation Tracker works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Knowledge Propagation Tracker does and why archives need it. Real trackers build a reuse graph from citation links, text-reuse detection (near-duplicate passage matching), and dataset derivation records, then run forward traversals from any fact to list every downstream reuse. When a correction lands, the tracker computes the correction cascade — all affected downstream nodes — and reports which have been updated and which still carry the old version. Each reuse edge cites its evidence (quote, citation, derivation log). Advanced systems detect paraphrased reuse with embedding similarity, handle versioned reuses (which edition copied which), and measure propagation speed and reach. Quality is measured by reuse-detection recall on known republication chains. The limits are uncredited copying with heavy rewriting — flagged as suspected-reuse with similarity scores rather than asserted — and offline reuse (print, word of mouth) that leaves no trace, which the tracker honestly reports as beyond its visibility.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
